What it covers: Purpose of the guide, a definition of business architecture (holistic views of capabilities, end-to-end value delivery, information and organisation, and how they relate to strategies, products, policies, initiatives and stakeholders), ten domains, three framework components, six principles and the strategy execution path.
How this template applies it: Chapters 0 and 6 set purpose and scope.

What it covers: The baseline views of the business. Four foundational views (capability, organisation, value, information) are stable; five extended views (strategy, initiative, product, stakeholder, policy) change more often. Guild advice: start with value mapping or capability mapping, use organisation mapping to set scope in complex structures, and treat information mapping as following the capability map.
How this template applies it: Each blueprint has a register or chapter section, see rows 2.1 to 2.9.

What it covers: How strategy, goals, objectives and courses of action are mapped and tied to the rest of the architecture. Covers principles (a strategy belongs to a community of interest; it responds to the external environment), benefits (alignment, fidelity of objectives, early gap detection) and frameworks: Ansoff grid, SWOT, Five Forces, Kaplan-Norton strategy map, Business Motivation Model, Hoshin Kanri.
How this template applies it: Objectives and vision; strategy to capability trace in requirements.

What it covers: Defining, building and using a capability map: capabilities named as nouns, kept stable, grouped by domain, and cross-mapped to value streams, organisation, information and initiatives.
How this template applies it: Capabilities register and capability map.

What it covers: Mapping organisational structure into the architecture, business units to capabilities, plus internal and external parties, so ownership and accountability are visible.
How this template applies it: Stakeholders and RACI registers.

What it covers: Value streams and value stream stages: how a stakeholder gets value end to end, and which capabilities enable each stage. Often delivered before the capability map because it is faster.
How this template applies it: Value stream register and flow diagram.

What it covers: A business view of information: concepts and their relationships, independent of systems, linked to capabilities and value stream stages.
How this template applies it: Data entities, dictionary, conceptual model.

What it covers: Showing initiatives against the capabilities, value streams and objectives they affect, so scope and overlap are visible.
